solved.topic: Nernst equation - cell EMF at non-standard concentration
solved.q: For the cell Zn | Zn2+(0.1 M) || Cu2+(1 M) | Cu, calculate the EMF at 298 K given E°cell = 1.10 V. (n = 2)
steps: Formula: Ecell = E°cell - (0.0591/n) log Q, where Q = [Zn2+]/[Cu2+] for the cell reaction Zn + Cu2+ -> Zn2+ + Cu.
Substitution: Q = 0.1/1 = 0.1, so log Q = log(10^-1) = -1.

solved.topic: Kohlrausch's law - limiting molar conductivity of weak electrolyte
solved.q: Calculate the limiting molar conductivity of CH3COOH given Lambda°(CH3COONa) = 91.0, Lambda°(HCl) = 426.2 and Lambda°(NaCl) = 126.5 S cm^2 mol^-1.
steps: Given: Lambda°(CH3COONa) = 91.0, Lambda°(HCl) = 426.2, Lambda°(NaCl) = 126.5 (all S cm^2 mol^-1).
Formula: Lambda°(CH3COOH) = Lambda°(CH3COONa) + Lambda°(HCl) - Lambda°(NaCl) (Kohlrausch's law of independent migration).

steps: Given: Lambda(m) = 48.15 S cm^2 mol^-1, Lambda°(m) = 390.7 S cm^2 mol^-1.

solved.q: A current of 5 A is passed through molten AgNO3 for 1930 seconds. Calculate the mass of silver deposited at the cathode (Ag = 108, F = 96500 C/mol).
steps: Given: I = 5 A, t = 1930 s, M(Ag) = 108 g/mol, n = 1 (Ag+ + e- -> Ag), F = 96500 C/mol.
Formula: Q = I x t; moles of electrons = Q/F; mass = (moles of electrons / n) x M.
Calculation: moles of Ag = 0.1/1 = 0.1 mol; mass = 0.1 x 108 = 10.8 g.
Answer: Mass of silver deposited = 10.8 g.

solved.topic: Faraday's law - time required for electrolysis
solved.q: Calculate the time required to deposit 10.8 g of silver from AgNO3 solution using a current of 0.5 A (Ag = 108, F = 96500 C/mol).
steps: Given: mass = 10.8 g, M(Ag) = 108 g/mol, n = 1, I = 0.5 A, F = 96500 C/mol.
Formula: moles of Ag = mass/M; moles of electrons = n x moles of Ag; Q = moles of electrons x F; t = Q/I.
Calculation: moles of electrons = 1 x 0.1 = 0.1 mol; Q = 0.1 x 96500 = 9650 C.
Answer: t = 19300 s = 5 hours 21 minutes 40 seconds (≈5.36 hours).
